text:
maria: Quick thread — we need a crisp decision on precedence for header-based region hints vs route-config failover. Planning: zone-drain + cold-standby for eu-west.
devin: TL;DR proposal: header `X-Redwood-Region` honored only for internal tokens or when header signed by our edge proxy. Otherwise ignore and use geo/route policies. :thinking_face:
kevin: Strong +1 on requiring signed header. Also we should have an explicit audit counter when header overrides actual geolocation (telemetry: `header_override_count`).
jen: From product POV we want a console toggle: "Allow header-based routing for admin calls" with an explain link. We need clear UX so customers don't accidentally route to a cold standby and blow cost.
maria: Agree. Also need rules for zone draining: when a zone is marked draining, route should shift traffic to local zone fallback, then to configured failover region, then to cold-standby. Can we express fallback order in route config? Example idea:
```yaml
route: /v1/generate
policy:
  geo_affinity: prefer-local
  fallback_order:
    - local_zone
    - region_failover: eu-central-1
    - cold_standby: eu-west-3
  header_override_allowed: admin_only
```
devin: That config looks ok. Implementation note: route matching must run before header validation. If a customer sets a route-level `region_failover`, it should be considered part of match scoring, not as a header override. We should unify score: preferHeader? No.
kevin: Implementation detail: when draining, we should tag sessions with `x-rw-routing-reason: zone-drain` so logs and tracing show why a region was ejected. Add metric `route_ejects.zone_drain` and histogram for added latency when failover happens.
infra-bot: NOTE: deploy v2 of apigw-routing-service scheduled 2026-04-03 02:00 UTC. Will add new header validation hooks.
maria: Good. We also need safety: fallback should respect per-customer quotas and SLOs. If failover target has limited capacity, either throttle or spill to a cheaper region. Rule: never exceed tenant reserved capacity in target region.
jen: UX question: should console show a simulated route trace? e.g., input client IP + optional header -> list of chosen region and why. That would help SRE and customers validate configs.
devin: Love the simulator. We can reuse existing routing telemetry and add a `routing_simulator` endpoint in the internal console. Keep it internal behind `allow_simulations` feature flag.
kevin: Tests: add e2e that simulates zone failure and asserts KV cache invalidation across failover, and that `x-rw-routing-reason` is populated. Also chaos test for header-spoof attempts.
maria: Security: header override must be signed with `X-RW-Sig` computed with edge key. If missing, treat header as untrusted. Example check in pseudo:
```python
if header and token.is_admin() and verify_sig(header, X_RW_Sig):
    use_header()
else:
    ignore_header()
```
devin: One more nuance — path-based route matching and header-based hints can both apply. We should add final tie-breaker rules: 1) match weight, 2) forced route override (explicit `force_region: true` in route config), 3) signed header (admin), 4) geo-affinity.
jen: For product copy: "Force region" is scary. We should label it "Route pinned region (use with care)" and require a checkbox + justification in console.
kevin: Telemetry list to add: `header_override_count`, `force_region_used`, `route_ejects{zone,region}`, `failover_latency_p50/p90/p99`, `simulator_runs`.
maria: Ops playbook: when failover triggers, send alert if p95 latency > target or if `route_ejects` > threshold. Also auto-rollout revert to previous routing policy if error rate spikes.
devin: I'll draft the routing PR with these precedence rules and add the header sig verification. Will include simulator endpoint + unit tests.
jen: Thanks — once PR is up, can we demo simulator in next platform sync? I'll prep the copy for the console toggle and warning modal.
deploy-bot: apigw-routing-service:v2 rollout started by devin — tracked in #eng-releases
kevin: small follow-up: confirm cold-standby billing alerts. We don't want customers unknowingly routed to an expensive standby. Add `billing_route_switch` metric and alert when standby used > 5% traffic for > 1h.
maria: noted. OK team — devin, assign me a review for the PR. I'll add tests for telemetry and the console team can start on the simulator stub.
devin: assigning now. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
